statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-9403: a reachable assertion in run_jq_tests() in src/jq_test.c, the code behind jq --run-tests, when a test's expected value is NaN (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/issues/3393). Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/a4d9d540103ff9a262e304329c277ec89b27e5f9 (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/pull/3408), first released in jq 1.8.2 (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/tag/jq-1.8.2); Debian rates it unimportant and records no fixed version (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-9403). Checked every jq build in the DHI Debian 13 repository for amd64 and arm64, using the changelog each package ships and its libjq: rebuilds of Debian 1.7.1-6+deb13u1 and 1.7.1-6+deb13u2, a 1.8.1-5 build (arm64 only) whose changelog is an unreleased Debian 1.8.1-5 snapshot from January 2026 with no 2026 security fixes, and a rebuild of Debian 1.8.2-1, which is upstream jq 1.8.2. The DHI rebuilds of Debian 1.7.1-6+deb13u1 and 1.7.1-6+deb13u2 add the fix; their changelogs list CVE-2025-9403. Ran jq --run-tests on one test that expects nan with the arm64 builds: the 1.7.1 rebuilds and the rebuild of 1.8.2-1 report a failed test and exit 1, while the 1.8.1-5 build aborts on the assertion at src/jq_test.c:204. The range therefore closes at the first 1.7.1-6+deb13u2 rebuild, reopens at 1.8.1-5 and closes again at the rebuild of 1.8.2-1. The rebuild of 1.7.1-6+deb13u1, which carries the fix too, sorts below the first boundary and reads as affected.
